item.title: [Wed, Jun 10] Town Talk: Can we change the weather (and do we really want to?)
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Innovation Center This town talk will be presented by Derek Posselt, Principal Scientist, NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory. If you live on planet Earth, you have had to worry about the weather at some point. Most of us have heard some version of the expression: “If you don’t like the weather, wait 5 minutes, and it will change.” Many of us wish we had the ability to do something about it. This is not a new impulse. Humans have been trying to change the weather for over a century. Posselt will review the ways people have tried to modify the weather, what has worked (and what hasn’t), and whether it is, in fact, a good idea to try in the first place.

item.title: [Mon, Jun 8] The Box: How Anxiety, Perfectionism, and People-Pleasing Kept Me Trapped at WPL
item.description:
🎫 KOTO
Join us on Monday, June 8th at 5:30 for a talk by well-being strategist, high-performance coach, bestselling author, and speaker Wendy Robbins ! The Box: How Anxiety, Perfectionism, and People-Pleasing Kept Me Trapped — and the Steps That Set Me Free You built the walls. You have the key. What if the anxiety, perfectionism, and people-pleasing you've spent your life managing aren't your greatest liabilities — but your biggest untapped assets? For over 40 years, Wendy Tamis Robbins hid in plain sight. From the outside, she had everything: Ivy-League grad, Div. 1 Athlete, Big Law attorney. On the inside, she was living with chronic anxiety, OCD, panic disorder, depression, substance abuse, and suicidal ideation — managing it all behind a flawless performance of having it all together. Then came a colon cancer diagnosis. And instead of breaking her, it broke her open. …

In this special space we give the water, fire and tea leaves a chance to communicate with us in their subtle and silent tongue. item.title: ‘Passages in Time’
item.description: Artist Micheline Klagsbrun is showing new resin sculptures and paper works at Fringe Gallery alongside longtime neighbor Nancy B. Frank's "Earth Gems" paintings. Klagsbrun's pieces incorporate local elements like elk bone found in the San Juans, while Frank has shifted from her well-known equine work to close-up geological abstractions inspired by photo trips to places like the Grand Canyon and even a Montrose cornfield.

item.title: ’Jacks prominent amongst kings
item.description: The Telluride High lacrosse team's senior defensive core, nicknamed the "Lumberjacks," wrapped up four years playing together with another strong season that included a first-place regular season finish and state tournament run. The Miners fell to Grand Junction 9-7 in the state quarterfinals, ending their season, but several players earned all-state honors including Henry Deppen and Leyton Holbrook on the first team.

item.title: A song for San Juan springtime
item.description: Southwest Colorado sits along major flyway corridors, bringing waves of neo-tropical birds from late April through early June - songbirds, warblers, swallows and raptors returning to summer territory, with hummingbirds testing gravity around every spring flower. The area around San Miguel County hosts 11,000-15,000 elk according to Parks and Wildlife, and watching the annual cycle of pregnant cows disappearing into sheltered woods before emerging with gangly calves remains one of spring's reliable miracles.

item.title: Commissioners approve Accelerated Housing Review
item.description: County commissioners approved fast-track review for affordable housing projects to qualify for state funding from Proposition 123's housing fund. Projects with 50% or more affordable units will get decisions within 90 days, but the same approval standards and review processes still apply. Some stakeholders had concerns about no size limits on eligible projects, though others supported accessing the available state money.

item.title: ‘If it took a leap of faith, I was willing’
item.description: Town officials met secretly with Chuck Horning's son Chad in December about buying Telski, leading to the controversial California trip that resulted in three resignations this year. An independent investigation cleared former Mayor Prohaska and Town Manager Wisor of wrongdoing, though they acknowledged the meetings were poorly handled and ultimately unsuccessful.

item.title: The beauty of unsafe seats
item.description: Safe legislative districts where primaries decide winners have created a system where party loyalists control outcomes while independents can't even vote in most states. This has pulled candidates toward ideological extremes, leading to legislative paralysis and opening doors for authoritarians who promise to cut through the gridlock. Competitive districts would shift focus back to pragmatic problem-solving and consensus-building, potentially restoring the legislative branch's ability to function through normal constitutional processes.

item.title: What to know about new trials ordered for two paramedics in the death of Elijah McClain
item.description: An appeals court ordered new trials for two paramedics convicted in Elijah McClain's 2019 death, saying the trial judge gave faulty jury instructions about the standard of care required. The paramedics had injected the 23-year-old with ketamine after police restrained him following a 911 call about someone "sketchy," leading to his cardiac arrest and death days later. Colorado's attorney general plans to appeal to the state supreme court, which could further delay any retrials.

item.title: Lady Miners emerge as all-leaguers
item.description: The Lady Miners lacrosse team had their most successful season yet, finishing 6-2 in league and 10-5 overall before losing in the first round of state playoffs. Five players earned All-League honors, with Ruby Lake and Mikayla Ialeggio also receiving All-State recognition. The new coach emphasized how the team's chemistry and enthusiasm set this group apart from previous years.

item.title: We got us a posse
item.description: Montrose County's volunteer sheriff's posse is looking for more help, especially on the West End where fewer than 20 people are available to respond to search and rescue, fires, and emergencies across a huge territory. The all-volunteer group saves taxpayers money by handling everything from medical assists to crowd control, but they're stretched thin as recreational use grows in the region.

item.title: San Miguel County finalizes deed restriction reversions
item.description: San Miguel County commissioners have finalized a process allowing certain deed-restricted homeowners to revert to earlier versions of their property covenants after years of what some called coercive covenant changes during sales transactions. Of 206 properties reviewed, 31 owners chose to switch back to previous deed restrictions, with the county acknowledging "unintentional mistakes" in how they administered the housing program that began in 2010 and was amended multiple times through 2023.

item.title: All hail the queen
item.description: A local writer shares the story of a garter snake queen who claimed territory beneath a concrete slab, emerging each morning to sun herself on the lawn and raising babies over several summers. The homeowner carefully worked around her domain during mowing and trimming, but this year she hasn't appeared. These quiet wildlife dramas play out all around us if we pay attention.

item.title: Homicide convictions reversed for Colorado paramedics who injected ketamine into Elijah McClain
item.description: A Colorado appeals court overturned homicide convictions for two Aurora paramedics who injected ketamine into Elijah McClain in 2019, ordering new trials while upholding one assault conviction. The case, which resulted in rare criminal charges against first responders, has sent ripples through emergency medical services nationwide as paramedics now face potential legal consequences for split-second decisions during police custody situations.

item.title: Open letter to council
item.description: A retired developer with experience on major projects is urging town council to get professional cost estimates before approving the parking and affordable housing projects currently being designed by Design Workshop. The letter writer warns that neither Design Workshop nor town staff have the capability to accurately forecast construction costs, and argues council shouldn't approve projects without knowing what residents will be paying for in debt service.

item.title: Medically overweight or obese isn't healthy for pets
item.description: More than half of North American pets are overweight or obese, creating health risks like arthritis, diabetes and shortened lifespans. The local animal shelter offers a simple at-home test using your hands to check your pet's body condition by feeling their ribs. Bailey, a one-eyed shelter cat, is currently on a weight management plan and available for adoption.

item.title: Vote for Marya Stark
item.description: This appears to be a brief endorsement letter for Marya Stark's town council campaign, though the text has some formatting issues that make parts unreadable. The endorser mentions Stark's focus on preserving Telluride's character, local housing, economic strength, and inclusive governance.

item.title: Get your glow on
item.description: The Telluride Balloon Festival's main event happens Saturday evening June 6, when eight tethered hot air balloons will glow along Colorado Avenue from 6-10 p.m. Families can get close to the balloons and even climb into baskets for photos. Weather permitting, 15 balloons will also launch early Saturday and Sunday mornings from Town Park, flying low over downtown before landing near the Valley Floor.

item.title: Telluride Elks Lodge celebrates 125 years
item.description: The Telluride Elks Lodge is marking 125 years with 260 members across the region, operating out of the historic Swede-Finn Hall on Pacific Avenue. They've doubled their scholarship awards to $9,000 this year for six students pursuing any post-high school education, and continue hosting longtime community events like Turkey Bingo and Huck Finn Day.
